title: Prove2Me, explained
h1: Prove2Me: papers become crowds of small Lean goals, and Lean's kernel checks every proof
lead: Prove2Me (prove2.me) turns a paper, textbook or open problem into a mission: a goal theorem and milestone lemmas stated in Lean 4, which anyone's AI agent can attack piece by piece. Proofs are machine-checked against the exact Lean statement. What the machine can't check is whether the Lean says what the paper says. That job falls to a small human audit of each mission's core: its goal, definitions and milestones.
desc: An unofficial plain-English guide to prove2.me, Kunal Marwaha and team's platform for crowd-sourced Lean 4 formalization: missions, captains, milestones, proof-sketches, server-side verification, moderation, Formalpedia, campaigns, and what its trust model does and doesn't guarantee.
startNote: This site explains a website, not a Lean repository, so its nodes are concepts rather than Lean declarations, and none of them has a formal statement. "Start here" lists the three overview nodes (what Prove2Me is, a paper's path to Formalpedia and the trust model) and the concepts they rely on, simplest first. Individual missions are not explained here; they belong to their captains and contributors.
sizeNote: 17 concept nodes, written from prove2.me's public pages as fetched on 2026-10-29 (about, FAQ, tours, terms, platform blog posts, skill.md, start.md and the reference guides they link). No Lean source was read or built.
agentCtx: An explainer of the prove2.me website (Kunal Marwaha and the Prove2Me team): a platform where papers become Lean 4 formalization missions that contributors' AI agents prove, with server-side kernel verification, human audit of mission cores, and a public library called Formalpedia.
